messages:
Alex: tossing another idea onto the windowed-index thread. instead of fixed-size windows, what if we used a logical 'activation frontier' that groups blobs by component boundaries (runtime, models, runtime-deps) so ops can activate only parts of the stack? reduces blast radius for model-only updates.

Sam: I like component grouping. couple concerns: 1) verification complexity (different component sets can have different trust roots) 2) rollout ordering inter-deps.

Maria: agreed on ordering. proposal: each component window has: component_id, seq, merkle_root, signer_meta, depends_on: [component:seq]. Operator resolver builds a DAG and activates leaves first. nodes write per-component activation markers.

Jin: compatibility with current onprem agent — today it's single manifest + single activation. we can make top-level manifest carry a components array. older agents would treat unknown keys as opaque and fall back to full apply (safer). new agent behavior: fetch component bundles in parallel, verify per-component root, verify cross-component dependency constraints, apply, write marker.

Priya: ops playbook thought: for model-only updates we can route traffic via canary set that only pulls model component. if runtime component isn't changing, we skip rolling runtime nodes. makes testing faster. need a way to express "no-op" dependency verifications for skipped components.

Sam: GC + retention: for components we should keep blobs until component_seq is superseded *and* no active cluster references older seqs. suggest adding `retain_until` map in manifest with cluster-scoped leases. operator only GC when all leases expire or are bumped.

Maria: security: multi-signer model means we need signer policies per-component. E.g., model artifacts signed by model-signing key, runtime signed by infra key. the agent must enforce signer namespace mapping. Jin, any perf hit verifying many signatures?

Jin: verifying N component signatures is cheap compared to applying model. but manifest bloat is real if we embed full sig blocks. options: 1) include compact signature envelopes (sig-id + sig-ref) and serve sigs via sidecar on demand, 2) use aggregated signature (BLS-ish) for whole manifest. both need spec.

Alex: rough UX: manifest_v3 componentized schema. operator constructs DAG, signs per-component, publishes manifest. agent flags: `--component-mode=on` and `--verify-signer-map=/etc/signer_map.json`. rollout steps: create manifest, stage to staging cluster, enable resume + activation markers, canary model-only, then widen. rollback: operator flips target_seq back and publishes "revoke" marker; agents must support idempotent rollback apply.

Priya: question: revoke marker semantics? do we require agents to garbage-collect applied blobs on revoke? risky on disk space. maybe revoke only flips active seq; agent keeps blobs until GC passes.

Sam: agree. revoke should be logical only. physical deletion gated by retention policy. also need metrics: per-component apply time, verify time, activation latency.

Maria: action items: Jin to draft signer-envelope + compact-sig proposal, Sam to draft GC lease/retain_until spec, Priya to mock operator CLI for component DAG staging, Alex to sketch manifest_v3 example and bring to arch sync. deploy-bot: created branch `componentized-manifest` and queued integration job -> https://ci.internal/repo/componentized-manifest/782

deploy-bot: CI: job 782 started, 12 tests queued

Alex: thanks all. we'll iterate on the signer and GC drafts before the Friday sync.
